currentContext.business: Borosil Renewables Limited manufactures low-iron textured solar glass, a key component used in making solar photovoltaic modules for power generation, from a technologically advanced facility at Bharuch, Gujarat. Part of the Borosil Group with a legacy of over six decades in consumer, scientific and laboratory glassware, the Company serves solar module manufacturers in India and exports to Europe, Turkey, the Americas and the MENA region, and has extended its glass into greenhouse, anti-glare and Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) applications. During FY 2025-26 it also entered the rooftop solar segment with Borosil-branded panels, inverters and battery storage sold through a direct-to-customer and a distribution channel.

currentContext.expansion: Borosil Renewables' expansion is concentrated at its single flagship solar-glass complex at Bharuch, Gujarat, a 100-acre site described as India's first and largest solar glass facility. The company's capacity has been built in steps: India's first solar glass line of 180 TPD in 2010, expansion to 450 TPD (equivalent to 2.8 GW/annum) in 2019, and a further 550 TPD addition in 2023 taking India capacity to a total of 1,000 TPD (equivalent to 6.5 GW per annum). The AR's combined-installed-capacity chart traces the same path across furnaces - Furnace 1 (India) 240 TPD, Furnace 2 (India) 210 TPD, Furnace 3 (India) 550 TPD, plus Furnace 1 (Europe) - from 180 TPD in CY18 to 1,000 TPD at July CY25, with 1,600 TPD shown as the Est CY26 position. The live project is the 600 TPD expansion designated SG 4&5, on which work was commenced during 2025. The company states the 600 TPD project entails an investment of Rs 950 crores and is targeted for completion by December 2026; once operational, total installed capacity will increase to 1,600 TPD, enabling it to support approximately 10.5 GW of solar module demand annually - described in the report as 'Combined Solar Glass Capacity Planned: 1600 TPD (~10.5 GW)'. The expansion is funded from a 2025 preferential issue of equity shares and warrants raising Rs 517.66 crores plus an additional Rs 371.49 crores, explicitly earmarked to expand production capacity by 60% at the Bharuch facility. Alongside glass capacity, the company invested in a second captive power plant of 16.5 MW of wind-solar hybrid generation under a group captive mechanism with high plant load factor; this plant achieved commercial operations in March 2026 (against an expectation of September 2025) and allows the company to meet about 75% of its power requirement from green energy while reducing power cost. On the product-mix side, the share of 2 mm glass production was raised to 75% with the stated aim of reaching 100% by Q4 FY 2026-27, and grid-printed glasses for bifacial modules were successfully introduced. Product/application widening also continues into greenhouse glass, anti-glare glass and Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV). Working against this domestic build-out, the European footprint has been exited rather than expanded: step-down subsidiary GMB Glasmanufaktur Brandenburg GmbH discontinued production and filed for insolvency on July 04, 2025, and its holding company Geosphere Glassworks GmbH filed for insolvency on December 22, 2025, with the Board writing off the Rs 32,590.81 lakhs exposure; the Europe furnace consequently drops out of the combined capacity chart. Demand-side context cited for the expansion is India adding a record ~44.6 GW of solar capacity in FY 2025-26 and cumulative solar installed capacity crossing 150 GW (150.26 GW as of March 31, 2026), against domestic solar glass production currently estimated at around 18 GW and expected to increase sharply to nearly 51 GW by FY 2026-27 as new capacities by existing and new entrants commence operations.

risks.risk: Competition from dumped/low-priced Chinese solar glass and duty circumvention through third countries
risks.note: China accounts for over 96% of total global solar glass capacity. Following anti-dumping duties on solar glass imports from China and Vietnam in December 2024, import patterns shifted rather than stopped — production has increasingly moved to Malaysia and Indonesia, which are not currently subject to such duties. Management also flags trans-shipment through Southeast Asian hubs and inventory dumping as practices that may undermine trade protections, distort pricing and disrupt fair competition, and the possibility that Chinese manufacturers set up production facilities in other countries to access key markets like India.

risks.risk: Dependence on policy and trade-remedy support; adverse shifts in incentives or compliance requirements
risks.note: Management states that policy and regulatory developments remain critical, as shifts in incentives or compliance requirements may directly influence pricing, project economics and profitability. Structural support currently comes from ALMM, Basic Customs Duties and the anti-dumping/countervailing duties the Company championed; timely policy intervention is repeatedly cited as necessary to safeguard domestic manufacturers, including against surplus Chinese capacity being redirected to India during prolonged US-China tariff tensions.

risks.risk: Emergence of integrated module players with captive solar glass capacity
risks.note: Within the solar glass sector, the emergence of integrated players with captive capacities creates the risk of sporadic supply of surplus production entering the open market, triggering price-based competition and margin pressures. Management separately notes that as large players increasingly shift toward captive consumption, surplus capacities are driving pricing pressures alongside aggressive tariff bidding.

risks.risk: Missing upstream domestic value chain (polysilicon, ingots, wafers) exposing the sector to input supply and pricing shocks
risks.note: Capacity in upstream segments such as polysilicon, ingots and wafers remains non-existent in India and continues to evolve; any gaps in these critical inputs could expose the sector to supply chain disruptions and pricing pressures, particularly from Chinese suppliers. Management expects ingot and wafer exposure to ease over the next 2-3 years as new capacities are set up, but states the threat still continues in the case of polysilicon — relevant because ALMM List-III will require domestic wafers and ingots by 2028.

risks.risk: Single-product, single-segment concentration in flat (solar) glass
risks.note: The Company's operations are focused on a single primary business segment, the manufacture of flat glass, with no separate reportable segments under Ind AS 108; revenue is disclosed only on a geographical basis. Earnings therefore track one product's pricing cycle, which is the same cycle exposed to import dumping and captive-capacity surplus.

risks.risk: Weak European module manufacturing base undermining the Company's European operations
risks.note: In Europe, policy implementation gaps have led to the closure of several module manufacturing facilities as cheap imports of solar modules flood the markets, weakening competitiveness. This is a direct demand risk for the Company's European furnace, and Europe/Turkey lead its exports. In the United States, trade tensions intensified in April 2026 with triple-digit anti-dumping duties (123.04%) on solar imports from India and Southeast Asian hubs.

risks.risk: Geopolitical instability in the Middle East disrupting fuel and freight
risks.note: Geopolitical risks in the Middle East cause supply chain issues for critical inputs like oil & gas, raise commodity prices, increase freight costs and delay critical component deliveries. Disruptions to critical fuel supply routes have caused problems including escalating prices — material for an energy-intensive furnace operator.

risks.risk: Cyber security and data privacy exposure
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a negative-implication risk: any compromise of customer privacy or data security may result in reputational harm, missed business opportunities and increased legal exposure; cybersecurity incidents can interrupt operations, expose sensitive information and lead to financial losses from litigation, regulatory penalties and remediation costs. Cyber Security is among the top enterprise-level risks reviewed by the Board's Risk Management Committee.

one-line thesis: A strong, price-and-protection-driven quarter: standalone sales +53% YoY to Rs 405.69 cr with EBITDA at 35% (Rs 142 cr) — a 4th straight quarter above 33% — as anti-dumping/CVD walls (China/Vietnam ADD since Dec-24; Malaysia CVD 9.71% extended 5 yrs) plus a domestic supply gap (local solar glass meets only ~25% of demand) hold import-parity pricing, while a fuel surcharge (Rs 9.50/sqm from 10-Mar-26) offsets the West-Asia-war energy spike. Plants ran at full 1,000 TPD; a new solar-wind hybrid captive lifted renewable power to 93% (~Rs 18 cr/yr savings). The core catalyst is the **600 TPD expansion (1,000→1,600 TPD, +60%)** — construction done by Dec-26, both furnaces (SG4/SG5) commissioned by Mar-27, revenue from FY28, adding ~Rs 80-85 cr incremental EBITDA/quarter. Management aspires to grow from ~Rs 2,500 cr to Rs 4,000 cr+ in 3-4 years and is deciding the next furnace/adjacency within ~6 months. Note the reported PAT optics: Q4FY26's Rs 169 cr carried a Rs 75 cr one-off tax write-back (German write-off), so the QoQ "profit halving" to ~Rs 87 cr is an artifact, not operational decay.

> Optics to watch: (1) QoQ PAT "drop" to ~Rs 87 cr is purely the Rs 75 cr Q4 tax write-back reversing out — operations are flat-to-up QoQ (EBITDA Rs 144.61→Rs 142 cr). (2) The Rs 160 realization is inflated by the Rs 9.50 fuel surcharge, which will compress (and is already being trimmed) as fuel costs ease — neutral to profit since costs fall in tandem.

- **600 TPD expansion (1,000→1,600 TPD, +60% capacity):** construction complete by **Dec-26**, both furnaces (SG4 + SG5, ~1-month gap) commissioned **by Mar-27 (Q4 FY27)**; model revenue from **1-Apr-27 / FY28** (internal target 1-Mar; management advises conservative FY28). → **sales +60%; incremental EBITDA ~Rs 80-85 cr per quarter** at current prices.
- **Rooftop solar (solar-kit) revenue: ~Rs 36 cr for FY27** (Q1 did ~Rs 1.3 cr); single-digit EBITDA (trading, not 30-35% manufacturing).

- **Fuel surcharge (Rs 9.50) to compress / be passed back** as fuel costs ease (profit-neutral — cost falls too).

- **Rooftop solar-kit (new):** module+inverter+battery on-grid residential system (2-3 states first, then C&I); brand-leverage play; trading economics (single-digit EBITDA); ~Rs 36 cr FY27 target.
- **Overseas (Germany — Geosphere / GMB):** investment written off (Rs 325 cr); insolvent; ~nil revenue — the historic EBITDA drag (-Rs 23 cr YoY quarter) is essentially gone.

- **Next furnace (600/1,200 TPD) or glass adjacency** — decision in ~6 months; path to Rs 4,000 cr+.
- **Rooftop solar-kit** — small now, but "much bigger opportunity in turnover" if volumes scale.
- **US market** — future optionality, negligible today.
- **Policy tailwinds:** ALMM 2 (cells, 1-Jun-26), ALMM 3 (ingot/wafer, from 28-Jun) deepen the domestic PV chain and pull solar-glass demand; EV/data-center/green-hydrogen as incremental demand drivers.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Only listed domestic solar-glass pure-play at scale** into a structural supply gap (domestic ~25% of demand) — import-parity pricing power evidenced by +53% value on +8% volume.
- **Trade-remedy moat:** ADD on China/Vietnam (Dec-24) + Malaysia CVD 9.71% (extended 5 yrs to 2031) cap import competition; reference price = landed import parity.
- **Cost/ESG edge:** 93% renewable captive power (~Rs 18 cr/yr savings) — a durable unit-cost advantage vs a fuel-exposed process.
- Management explicitly: "we don't foresee any kind of challenge on the pricing" even as domestic capacity rises to 7,700 TPD, because much of new capacity is captive and demand stays ~75% short.
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBITDA 35% (>33% for 4 straight quarters); gross margin ~78% (RM ~23-24%); no material RM/price volatility expected → EBITDA margin set to rise YoY in FY27 on full-year full-price realization (H1 FY26 was still ramping post-ADD).
- Fuel surcharge (Rs 9.50) offsets war-driven gas/oil spike; already being trimmed as fuel eases (profit-neutral pass-through, committed to customers).
- Renewable captive power (93%) structurally lowers energy cost.

- **600 TPD (SG4/SG5):** fully funded, layout frozen, building under construction; done Dec-26, commissioned by Mar-27, revenue FY28. Watch: 1-2 month furnace stabilization → management models revenue only from 1-Apr (conservative).

one-line thesis: A strong, price-and-protection-driven quarter: standalone sales +53% YoY to Rs 405.69 cr with EBITDA at 35% (Rs 142 cr) — a 4th straight quarter above 33% — as anti-dumping/CVD walls (China/Vietnam ADD since Dec-24; Malaysia CVD 9.71% extended 5 yrs) plus a domestic supply gap (local solar glass meets only ~25% of demand) hold import-parity pricing, while a fuel surcharge (Rs 9.50/sqm from 10-Mar-26) offsets the West-Asia-war energy spike. Plants ran at full 1,000 TPD; a new solar-wind hybrid captive lifted renewable power to 93% (~Rs 18 cr/yr savings). The core catalyst is the **600 TPD expansion (1,000→1,600 TPD, +60%)** — construction done by Dec-26, both furnaces (SG4/SG5) commissioned by Mar-27, revenue from FY28, adding ~Rs 80-85 cr incremental EBITDA/quarter. Management aspires to grow from ~Rs 2,500 cr to Rs 4,000 cr+ in 3-4 years and is deciding the next furnace/adjacency within ~6 months. Note the reported PAT optics: Q4FY26's Rs 169 cr carried a Rs 75 cr one-off tax write-back (German write-off), so the QoQ "profit halving" to ~Rs 87 cr is an artifact, not operational decay.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **600 TPD expansion (1,000→1,600 TPD, +60% capacity):** construction complete by **Dec-26**, both furnaces (SG4 + SG5, ~1-month gap) commissioned **by Mar-27 (Q4 FY27)**; model revenue from **1-Apr-27 / FY28** (internal target 1-Mar; management advises conservative FY28). → **sales +60%; incremental EBITDA ~Rs 80-85 cr per quarter** at current prices.
- **Rooftop solar (solar-kit) revenue: ~Rs 36 cr for FY27** (Q1 did ~Rs 1.3 cr); single-digit EBITDA (trading, not 30-35% manufacturing).

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
